name: le_dual
source: private theorem le_dual (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (N : Type) [AddCommGroup N] [Module ℤ_[l] N] :
Module.length ℤ_[l] N ≤ Module.length ℤ_[l] (N →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l) := by
change OrderDual.ofDual b < OrderDual.ofDual a at hab
obtain ⟨hle, m, hmp, hmq⟩ := SetLike.lt_iff_le_and_exists.mp hab
have h := LinearMap.congr_fun hφ ⟨x, hle hx⟩
exact hψ (by simpa using LinearMap.congr_fun hmem' ⟨m, hmp⟩)
show: For every prime ℓ and every ℤℓ-module N, the length of N is at most that of Hom(N,ℚℓ/ℤℓ), including infinite lengths.
strategy: Send each submodule to its annihilator in the dual and compare the dimensions of the submodule orders.

steps.claim: Write D(N) = Homℤℓ(N,ℚℓ/ℤℓ) and Ann(P) = {φ ∈ D(N) | φ vanishes on P}. Module length is the supremum of the lengths of finite chains of strict inclusions of submodules, unchanged by reversing the order. A strictly inclusion-reversing annihilator map therefore gives length(N) ≤ length(D(N)). For P ⊊ Q, choose m ∈ Q outside P.
steps.snippet:
Module.length ℤ_[l] N ≤ Module.length ℤ_[l] (N →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l) := by
  rw [← WithBot.coe_le_coe, Module.coe_length, Module.coe_length, ← Order.krullDim_orderDual]
  refine Order.krullDim_le_of_strictMono
    (fun p : (Submodule ℤ_[l] N)ᵒᵈ =>
      LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lcomp ℤ_[l] (QZ l) (OrderDual.ofDual p).subtype)) ?_
  intro a b hab
  change OrderDual.ofDual b < OrderDual.ofDual a at hab
  obtain ⟨hle, m, hmp, hmq⟩ := SetLike.lt_iff_le_and_exists.mp hab

steps.claim: For P ⊊ Q, one has Ann(Q) ⊊ Ann(P). Inclusion follows by restriction. To see strictness, a character on N/P nonzero at m+P pulls back to a member of Ann(P) outside Ann(Q).

children.claim: If φ vanishes on Q, then φ(x) = 0 for every x ∈ P because P ⊆ Q. Hence Ann(Q) ⊆ Ann(P).
children.snippet:
· intro φ hφ
    rw [LinearMap.mem_ker] at hφ ⊢
    ext ⟨x, hx⟩
    have h := LinearMap.congr_fun hφ ⟨x, hle hx⟩
    simpa using h

children.claim: Equality of the annihilators is impossible. Separation on N/P gives a character nonzero at m+P. Its pullback vanishes on P and is nonzero at m ∈ Q, whereas equality would force it to vanish there.
The class m+P in N/P is nonzero, since a quotient class is zero precisely when its representative lies in P and m was chosen outside P.
children.snippet:
have hm0 : (OrderDual.ofDual b).mkQ m ≠ 0 := by
      rwa [Ne, Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]

children.claim: Choose a character ψ on N/P such that ψ(m+P) ≠ 0, by separation of the nonzero class m+P.
Let π be the quotient N → N/P. For x ∈ P, π(x) = 0 and (ψ ∘ π)(x) = 0. Thus ψ ∘ π belongs to Ann(P).
children.snippet:
have hmem : ψ ∘ₗ (OrderDual.ofDual b).mkQ ∈
        LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lcomp ℤ_[l] (QZ l) (OrderDual.ofDual b).subtype) := by
      rw [LinearMap.mem_ker]
      ext ⟨x, hx⟩
      simp [(Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero _).mpr hx]
children.typedFact:
ψ ∘ₗ (OrderDual.ofDual b).mkQ ∈
        LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lcomp ℤ_[l] (QZ l) (OrderDual.ofDual b).subtype)

children.claim: If Ann(P) = Ann(Q), the character ψ ∘ π must vanish on Q and therefore at m ∈ Q. This would give ψ(m+P) = 0, contradicting its choice and proving strict inclusion.
children.snippet:
have hmem' := hmem
    simp only at heq
    rw [← heq, LinearMap.mem_ker] at hmem'
    exact hψ (by simpa using LinearMap.congr_fun hmem' ⟨m, hmp⟩)

chapterTitle: Twisted cokernels in a cyclotomic tower
